repos.name: muse-protocol
repos.description: muse.ai 注册与邀请码兑换协议研究（纯 HTTP Python 实现）
repos._readme:
# muse.ai 注册 / 邀请码兑换 协议分析

补充一下，记得用JP 节点， JP 不需要绑卡，直接过

纯 HTTP 实现 muse.ai 的注册与邀请码兑换流程，不依赖浏览器。本文记录的是通过抓包逐字段比对得出的协议细节。

## 快速开始

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp config.example.json config.json   # 填入邮箱与可选代理
python example_register.py
```

## 目录结构

```
musepy/
  client.py    注册 + 兑换的完整协议客户端
  runner.py    多账号批量调度（sticky 代理 / 预算 / 停止语义）
  otp.py       验证码轮询（幂等：只取 send 之后的最新码）
  falco.py     行为埋点上报（可选）
  caa.py       注册漏斗事件上报（可选）
example_register.py        单账号端到端示例
example_batch.py           多账号批量示例
config.example.json        配置模板
test_onboarding_smoke.py   离线冒烟（披露解析纯函数）
test_runner_smoke.py       离线冒烟（批量调度，mock 网络）
```

## 协议流程

```
GET  /                                   拿初始 cookie
POST /api/auth/native/restart            → 201 {csrf_token}
POST /api/auth/native/send-otp           → 201
POST /api/auth/native/confirm-otp        → 200 {registration_state:"completion_required",
                                               tos:{content_version}}（动态 TOS 版本）
POST /api/auth/native/register-completion→ 200 {auth_meta_session:{frl_access_token, frl_account_id}}
POST auth.meta.com/hatch/session/bootstrap/ → 302…→ muse.ai 200 HTML（会话引导，必须）
     └ 从 muse.ai 文档解析动态披露 disclosure_text/disclosure_version 与状态门
       （resolvedDestination/isGeoGated/waitlist → 地区受限）
POST /api/hatch/accept-tos               → 200（单次调用；正文用服务端动态披露，非硬编码）
GET  /api/hatch/invite                   → 200 表示账号有效
POST /api/hatch/vm/wake                  → 200（必须，否则兑换误报 invalid；
                                             wake_trigger=mount + open_id + away_ms=0）
POST /api/hatch/stateful-sharing         → 200
POST /api/hatch/invite-code/redeem       → 200 {redemptionStatus:"redeemed"}
POST /api/hatch/invite                   → 200 {code}（取回自己的码，不等于页面刮开 reveal）
```

## 几个容易踩的坑

### 1. `confirm-otp` 必须带 `supports_muse_link_transparency: true`

```json
{"otp_code":"123456","remember_device":true,"supports_muse_link_transparency":true}
```

### 2. `register-completion` 的姓名字段语义

```json
{
  "date_of_birth": "1993-11-14",
  "first_name": "三郎",     // 名（given name）
  "last_name": "近藤",      // 姓（family name）
  "tos_content_version": "ntm_create_account:default_v1_meta_account_v3+docs_v2",
  "remember_device": true
}
```

`first_name` 是名、`last_name` 是姓，与直觉相反。生日早于约 18 年前会返回 403——同一会话同一份姓名，只把生日从 2013 改成 1993 就能从 403 变 200。

### 3. `restart` 的 body 不是空对象

```json
{"resume": false}
```

### 4. `accept-tos` 是会话激活开关，且必须先引导会话

注册完成后**必须先走 `POST auth.meta.com/hatch/session/bootstrap/`**（form 表单只带
`frl_access_token`，手动跟随 302/301/303 跳转落到 muse.ai 200 文档），否则后续
hatch 接口一律 403。引导落地的 muse.ai 文档里带有 Next Flight 序列化的动态披露
（`disclosureText` / `disclosureVersion`，当前实测版本为 `HATCH_ROW_v0`），`accept-tos`
的正文必须用服务端返回的这份动态文案（**不是**硬编码常量），`Referer` 用披露页
URL；单次调用即可，不重试，403 时把响应体前 200 字符带出来便于诊断。

引导后若服务端判定 `resolvedDestination == "waitlist"` 或 `isGeoGated == true`，
属于**地区受限**：注册已完成、账号保留，但未证明已加入名单。

### 5. `vm/wake` 缺失会让兑换误报

不调 `vm/wake` 直接兑换，即使是有效码也会返回：

```json
{"success":false,"reason":"invalid","detail":"この招待コードは存在しません"}
```

需要先从已登录页面提取 `vmId`：

```python
re.search(r'vmId[\\"]*:[\\"]*([0-9a-fA-F-]{36})', html)
```

`wake` 的 body 实测为：`wake_trigger: "mount"`（首连）、`open_id`（新 uuid）、
`away_ms: 0`，而不是早期的 `resume`。

### 6. 兑换失败原因的含义

| reason | 含义 |
|---|---|
| `redeemed` | 成功 |
| `already_redeemed` | 本账号已经兑换过一个码 |
| `used_up` | 该码达到 30 次使用上限 |
| `invalid` | 码不存在，或没调 `vm/wake` |

## Cookie

注册成功后 `hatch_sess` 由 `register-completion` 的响应头下发（约 886 字符），这是后续所有 hatch 接口的凭证。`hatch_vml` 在注册阶段一直是被清空状态（`Max-Age=0`），不属于必需项。

## 多账号批量（musepy/runner.py）

```bash
python example_batch.py [count]
```

`config.json` 里的批量字段：

| 字段 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `otp_file` | 邮箱清单，每行 `email----otp源URL`（otp 源返回 `[{"otp","time"},...]` JSON） |
| `proxy_file` | sticky 代理池，每行 `host:port:user:pass`（或 `host:port`） |
| `codes_file` | 可选，待兑换邀请码池，每行一个 |
| `output_dir` / `tried_file` | 每账号结果 JSON 目录 / 已尝试邮箱清单 |
| `workers` / `max_per_ip` | worker 数（默认 5）/ 每条代理的验证成功上限（默认 6） |
| `resolve_ip` | 是否通过 ipify 解析出口 IP（默认 true） |
| `send_caa` | 批量模式

repos.description: ung220z-tool 是一个针对 UNG220Z（九联/Unionman 中国移动光猫）的一键凭据提取工具，仅限在你自己的设备上用于找回忘记的管理密码、迁移宽带配置或安全自查。
repos._readme:
# ung220z-tool

针对 **UNG220Z（九联 / Unionman 中国移动光猫）** 的一键凭据提取工具。

> ⚠️ 仅用于**你自己的设备**，用于找回自己忘记的管理密码、迁移宽带配置或安全自查。
> 未经授权对他人设备使用属于违法行为，作者不承担任何责任。

## 背景

这类光猫的 Web 管理页基于 `.gch` CGI 框架，登录口令由 TR-069 定期轮换，普通用户拿到的密码往往几天就失效。本工具走 Telnet 通道，直接读取设备配置库，拿到**当下有效**的全部凭据。

## 工作流程

```
用户输入账号密码
   ↓
拼出 http://<ip>/usr=<user>&psw=<pass>&cmd=1&telnet.gch 并打开浏览器（同时脚本直连兜底）
   ↓
Telnet 登录 → root shell
   ↓
sidbg 1 DB decry /userconfig/cfg/db_user_cfg.xml 解密配置
   ↓
提取 Web 账号 / Telnet 口令 / PPPoE / WiFi 密钥 / root 口令
   ↓
打印凭据表 + 落盘日志
```

## 用法

```bash
python3 ung220z.py
```

会依次询问：

```
※ 用户名和密码通常印在光猫【背面贴纸】上（S/N 标签）
  形如「用户名：user   密码：xxxxxxxx」，把光猫翻过来就能看到

① 光猫地址 [192.168.1.1]:
② 用户名 [user]:
③ 密码（输入时不显示）
   密码:
```

也可以全部走命令行：

```bash
python3 ung220z.py -i 192.168.1.1 -u user -p '你的密码'
python3 ung220z.py -i 192.168.1.1 -u user -p '你的密码' --no-browser
```

### 常用参数

| 参数 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `-i, --ip` | 光猫地址，默认 `192.168.1.1` |
| `-u, --user` | 登录用户名，默认 `user` |
| `-p, --password` | 登录密码，不填则交互输入 |
| `--telnet-user` | Telnet 用户名，默认 `CMCCAdmin` |
| `--telnet-password` | Telnet 口令（部分机型与 Web 口令不同） |
| `--no-browser` | 不调用浏览器，纯 HTTP 请求 |
| `--unlock` | Web 被会话锁占住时重启 httpd 解锁 |
| `--no-release` | 不尝试释放残留 Web 会话 |

## 输出示例

```
[22:15:00] INFO   会话开始  目标=192.168.1.1  账户=user
[22:15:00] HTTP   已发送给浏览器: http://192.168.1.1/usr=user&psw=***&cmd=1&telnet.gch
[22:15:00] HTTP   telnet.gch → TelnetSet Success!
[22:15:00] PROBE  nc -zv 192.168.1.1 23 → succeeded
[22:15:01] AUTH   Telnet CMCCAdmin / ****** → 登录成功（root）
[22:15:02] SHELL  sidbg 1 DB decry /userconfig/cfg/db_user_cfg.xml → /tmp/debug-decry-cfg
[22:15:03] DATA   DevAuthInfo  CMCCAdmin  / ******  Level=1
[22:15:04] CRACK  MATCH: ******  (/etc/shadow)
```

最后输出凭据汇总表，并写入 `ung220z_<时间戳>.log`。

## 依赖

- Python 3.8+
- 标准库即可，无需 pip 安装
- 设备已开启 Telnet（脚本会自动通过 `telnet.gch` 尝试开启）

## 原理说明

| 环节 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 开 Telnet | `GET /usr=<user>&psw=<pass>&cmd=1&telnet.gch`，返回 `TelnetSet Success!` 即成功 |
| Web 登录 | 密码前端只做 base64，`Frm_Logintoken` 每次响应递增，必须回填实时值 |
| 配置解密 | `sidbg 1 DB decry` 无口令即可解密，得到明文 XML |
| root 口令 | `/etc/shadow` 中为 SHA-256 crypt，工具会用常见出厂口令比对 |

## 免责声明

本项目仅用于教育与自有设备维护。使用者应确保对目标设备拥有合法管理权限。

# inference-optimisation An agent skill for **hill-climbing the speed of a local LLM server** on any hardware and any quantization. It covers: - single-user and concurrent decode - speculative decoding - prefill - KV cache size - startup time and time to first token It works under a memory cap, and every result has to survive a full-context stability check. It encodes how we actually got these speedups. It is not a list of flags. The workflow: 1. Compute the theoretical ceiling. 2. Change one thing at a time. 3. Measure against interleaved controls. 4. Log every result, including the failures. 5. Gate on long-context retrieval. 6. Qualify a clean, pinned build before publishing. It works with Claude Code and any agent that loads `SKILL.md`-style skills. Any model can also follow it from [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md). ## What we've been able to accomplish Results from the hill-climbs this skill was distilled from. Every number was measured on the hardware named; see the linked sources for methods and raw data. | Hardware | Model / quant / engine | Before → after | |---|---|---| | **Intel Arc B390 iGPU** (laptop, 64 GB unified LPDDR5X, ~115 GB/s) | Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B, EXL3 4 bpw, SGLang XPU + MTP | Decode, 1 user: 43.6 → **53 tok/s** (median)
Decode, 4 users: 84.7 → **103 tok/s**
Prefill 32K: 1,037 → **1,660 tok/s**
Prefill 256K: 297 → **628 tok/s** (2.1×)
KV cache: 264K tokens → **4 × 256K**
Startup: 113 → **43 s**
Registry Lab gates: decode 28.6 → **41.0**, prefill 255 → **667** | | **Intel Arc Pro B70** | Qwen3.8-27B, EXL3 4 bpw, vLLM + custom XPU kernels | Decode: **91.2 tok/s** at 1 user, **365** at 16 (prose, thinking on)
Same card with llama.cpp Q4_K_M: 25.0
Prefill 4K/32K/128K/254K: 1,654/1,434/928/650 → **2,421/2,259/1,415/911**
Agent-session replay: 193 → **147 s** | | **Intel Arc Pro B70** | Same model, SGLang + the same kernels | Decode, 1 user: **82.6 tok/s**, vs vLLM 75.7 on the same card and day | | **RTX 3090** | Qwen3.8-27B EXL3 3 bpw + MTP | **96.2 tok/s** prose / **141.1** code, 1 user | | **RTX 3090** | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B EXL3 3 bpw + MTP | **251.7 / 357.9 tok/s**, 1 user | | **RTX 3090** | Flash-Next EXL3, 256K context | MTP: 45.5 → **65.6 tok/s** | | **4× H200 NVL** | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, vLLM + speculative decoding | Crashed under load → **229.1 tok/s** decode, **17,546 tok/s** prefill; all six gates pass | Sources: - [local-ai-registry](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/local-ai-registry): - [Ornith B390 recipe](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/local-ai-registry/tree/main/data/sources/ornith-b390-exl3), with the full hill-climb log in [PR #453](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/local-ai-registry/pull/453) - the RTX 3090 and H200 recipes - [trellis-serve](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/trellis-serve): - `xpu/README.md`, `xpu/docs/PROGRESS.md` and `xpu/docs/SGLANG.md` for B70 - `cuda/README.md` for the RTX 3090 - [qwen-serve](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/qwen-serve) ### Reading the B390 result That run is the one this skill grew out of. Its ceiling calculation said: - **Decode:** 100 tok/s for one user was only reachable with two useful speculative drafts. This model's draft head accepts ~14% at depth 2, so the practical target was ~88–97 tok/s. We reached ~55% of it; the rest is GEMV kernel efficiency. - **Prefill at 256K:** we reached 628 tok/s against a ~670–684 tok/s ceiling. The skill makes the agent compute this up front, so it can tell you early when a target is above the physics. ## How it works ``` ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ measure HW ─▶ │ THEORY.md: bytes/token ÷ bandwidth, FLOPs/token ÷ 50% peak, KV │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ baseline ─▶ profile ─▶ pick lever (ceiling gap × likelihood) ─▶ configs/NEW.json ▲

repos.description: AI clipping for long videos and live streams. Self-hosted, bring your own AI key.
repos._readme:
# PeakCut

Turn long videos and live streams into captioned vertical clips, ready to post. Free and open source: run it on
your own computer or server, with your own AI key.

Paste a YouTube, Twitch or Kick link (or upload a file) and PeakCut finds the moments worth clipping, cuts them to
9:16, adds word-by-word captions and a hook, and can post them to your connected accounts. It can also record a
creator's live stream and clip the highlights while the stream is still running.

## What it does

- **Clips from any video.** Transcribes the audio, asks an AI which moments would hold a stranger's attention, and
  renders each one with captions in one of three styles.
- **Live clipping.** Records a stream into a rolling buffer and clips as it happens, using loudness, chat activity
  and the transcript.
- **Workspaces per creator.** Channels, clip settings, posting rules and an activity log for each creator you clip.
- **Posting.** Connect YouTube, Instagram and TikTok in one click, then queue or auto-post finished clips, with
  spacing and daily caps (see [DEPLOY.md](DEPLOY.md#connecting-youtube-instagram-and-tiktok) for the one-time setup).
- **No sign-in on your own computer.** It opens straight into the dashboard. On a shared server, switch accounts on
  (`PEAKCUT_ACCOUNTS=1`) for email or Google sign-in and an admin dashboard.
- **Your own AI.** Gemini, OpenAI, Grok, Groq, OpenRouter, Claude, a local model through Ollama, or anything that
  speaks the OpenAI chat format. No key at all also works: clips are then picked by loudness.

## Quick start

You need Python 3.10 or newer and `ffmpeg`. On Windows: `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg`. On a Mac: `brew install ffmpeg`.
On Linux: `sudo apt install ffmpeg`. PeakCut finds it by itself and tells you in the dashboard if it is missing.

Put PeakCut in a short folder that stays put: `C:\peakcut` on Windows, `~/peakcut` on a Mac or Linux. Not inside a
temporary folder or an AI assistant's workspace: those get cleaned up, and on Windows a folder that deep stops the
speech model from loading (Windows can't open files whose full path is over 260 characters). If an AI assistant
installs it for you, it should ask you where to put it first ([AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) tells it to).

On Windows:

```bash
git clone <this repository> C:\peakcut
```

```bash
cd C:\peakcut
```

On a Mac or Linux:

```bash
git clone <this repository> ~/peakcut
```

```bash
cd ~/peakcut
```

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Start the server:

```bash
python -m studio.server
```

The first start downloads the speech model by itself (about 480 MB, once).

Open http://127.0.0.1:8765. There is no sign-in: it opens straight into the dashboard. Go to **Settings, AI**, choose
your AI service, paste your key and press **Save and test** (see [Choose your AI](#choose-your-ai)).

## Choose your AI

PeakCut needs a chat model that can return JSON. The easy way is in the dashboard: **Settings, AI**. Pick the
service, paste your key, press **Find models** to choose from the service's own list, then **Save and test**. The
key is kept in the data folder on your machine and is never shown again.

# 🕹️ Spaceship IDE

Steer your ideas in realtime, space pilot style!

![Screencast](./extra/screencast.gif)

## Demos

Watch on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/reels/DfyQPhFtW-z/) and [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3WmNLWUmcnY). You can try the simulator at [https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/](https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/) with the option to go live with your API keys for Cerebras and Gemini. Keys stay in your browser local storage. Do it at your own risk.

## Conjecture

> In the near future, LLM and Decision Models will reach 60 FPS interactivity.

When that happens, what new interaction paradigms will unlock? This project demonstrates plausible and desirable interactions for that future.

1. **Focus monitor**: can we visualize what LLM is paying attention to, and use that to guide human's focus towards what's important?

   ![focus monitor](./extra/clips/focus-monitor.gif)

2. **Attention lock**: can we force LLM to pay more attention to specific phrases so as to bias its future behavior?

   ![attention lock](./extra/clips/attention-lock.gif)

3. **Future Vector Steering**: can we decompose the task into eigenvectors, independently tune each, and re-compose them to influence the incoming text?

   ![future steering](./extra/clips/future-steering.gif)

4. **Realtime re-generation**: when text generation is cheap and fast, can we explore alternative futures by scrubbing?

   ![realtime regeneration](./extra/clips/realtime-regeneration.gif)

## Design process

I used Claude Code for most of the implementation but stayed hands-on for the UI/UX. I iterate using interactive style swatch, a technique where I prompt AI to give me diverse options of designs, I provide feedback, and it iterates. You can see the design artifacts in the [extra page](https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/extra/style-1.html).

To achieve the realtime experience, I have to use agreesive speculative generation and manage cache invalidation based on user interactions. For example, when the main knob moves backward, I have to empty future texts and cancel ongoing requests. There are many considerations like this throughout the system and that took a lot of human judgement - claude didn't one shot them.

## Theory

I'm currently focusing on systems that help human shape ideas in realtime. This project is a small step towards my [upcoming thesis](https://code.chuanqisun.com/master-thesis/) at the MIT Media Lab, where I investigate how semantic and symoblic systems can be coupled to enhance human creativity, agency, and joy of craft.

## Citation

If you build on this work, please cite it as:

```bibtex
@misc{sun2026spaceship,
  author       = {Sun, Chuanqi},
  title        = {Spaceship {IDE}: Steer Your Ideas in Realtime, Space Pilot Style},
  year         = {2026},
  publisher    = {GitHub},
  howpublished = {\url{https://github.com/chuanqisun/spaceship}},
  note         = {Demo: \url{https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/}}
}
```

repos._readme:
# tiny-voca

tiny-voca is a small English text-to-speech model. It has two voices, 4.5M
parameters, and runs on a CPU or in the browser.

[Demo](https://tiny-voca.n4ze3m.com) · [Weights](https://huggingface.co/n4ze3m/tiny-voca) · [Dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/n4ze3m/tiny-voca)

## Features

- **Small**: 4,537,291 parameters, 18 MB, waveform generator included.
- **Fast**: about 70x real time on four CPU threads.
- **Two voices**: F2 (female) and M2 (male), American English, 24 kHz.
- **Runs anywhere**: PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, and ONNX Runtime Web.
- **Open**: code, weights, training recipe and dataset. Trained from scratch.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/n4ze3m/tiny-voca.git
cd tiny-voca
pip install -e ".[own]"
hf download n4ze3m/tiny-voca --local-dir weights
export DIZIONE_DATA=weights/phonemizer
```

## Usage

```bash
python -m tiny_voca.infer \
  --checkpoint weights/tiny-voca.pt \
  --voice F2 \
  --text "Hello! This is tiny voca." \
  --output hello.wav
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--text-file` | | Read the text from a file instead of `--text` |
| `--voice` | `F2` | `F2` or `M2` |
| `--speed` | 1.0 | Speaking rate |
| `--pitch-shift` | 0 | Raise or lower the pitch |
| `--pitch-range` | 1.0 | More or less pitch movement |

Long text is fine. It is read one sentence at a time and the audio is joined.
A text that ends without a mark gets a full stop, so the last word does not
break off. A sentence with nothing to read, such as one in another script, is
skipped. The output never peaks above 0.99, so it does not clip as a 16-bit
WAV. In Python, `tiny_voca.infer.speak_text` does the same.

## ONNX

```bash
python -m tiny_voca.export --checkpoint weights/tiny-voca.pt --output tiny-voca.onnx
```

A ready file is in the weights repository as `onnx/model.onnx`. The
[model card](https://huggingface.co/n4ze3m/tiny-voca) shows how to call it.

## Web demo

The [demo](https://tiny-voca.n4ze3m.com) runs the model in the browser. It
plays each sentence as soon as it is made, and keeps the whole clip in the
player. Its source is in `web/`.

```bash
cd web
bash fetch_assets.sh /path/to/dizione
npx wrangler dev
```

## Plain JavaScript

An experiment in `js/`: the model and the phonemizer in plain scripts, with no
libraries. It reads one 8 MB file and runs in the browser, in Node and in Bun.

```bash
node js/say.mjs "Hello! This is tiny voca." --voice M2 --output hello.wav
```

See [js/README.md](js/README.md).

## Training

```bash
export TINY_VOCA_FRONTEND=own
python -m tiny_voca.prepare --inputs data/train-*.parquet --split train --output features
python -m tiny_voca.annotate --features features --output annotations
python -m tiny_voca.train --train annotations/train.jsonl --validation annotations/validation.jsonl \
  --output runs/NAME --steps 104000 --gan-start 8000 --gan-ratio 0.7 --teacher-final 0
python -m tiny_voca.evaluate --checkpoint runs/NAME/inference.pt --annotations annotations --output eval/NAME
```

The released weights took 7.7 hours on one RTX 4090. More about the model and
the data is in [docs/model.md](docs/model.md).

## Tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src:tests python -m unittest discover -s tests
```

## Limits

- English only. Two fixed voices. No voice cloning.
- The F2 voice sounds younger than intended. A more mature voice is planned.
- Foreign names and odd spellings are often read wrong.
- No streaming yet.

## Community

Built by other people on top of tiny-voca.

Languages and voices:

- [apptor-tiny-tts](https://huggingface.co/apptor/apptor-tiny-tts): German.
- [tiny-voca-it](https://github.com/carbogninalberto/tiny-voca-it): Italian.
- [zerre-tts](https://github.com/erkinemreta1/zerre-tts): Turkish.
- [clarvia-tts-tiny](https://huggingface.co/wite-tech/clarvia-tts-tiny): Turkish, ten voices, with its own [phonemizer](https://huggingface.co/wite-tech/clarvia-phonemizer) for numbers, dates and money.
- [korean-tts](https://github.com/ooodev/korean-tts): Korean,

# dsh-superagent

> **Research prototype for reference only, not an official DeepSeek product.** This code grew out of our team's day-to-day development work, with much of the engineering done by coding agents. Treat it as research code, not production-ready software. It may still contain bugs, and its coding style and engineering practices may be inconsistent. Review and adapt it before using it in your own environment.
>
> We have adapted it for publication, so it is not identical to our internal version or the implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*. Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype.

dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/). It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.

It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's attention, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when someone must act or can use a result. [docs/000-philosophy.md](docs/000-philosophy.md) explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.

## Setup

Setup has many steps, so an agent does it with you. Ask your coding agent:

> Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me.

It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures everything. [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) is what it follows.

## Documentation

Read the numbered documents in order; each builds only on the ones before it.

- [000 Philosophy](docs/000-philosophy.md)
- [001 Domain model](docs/001-domain.md)
- [002 Authorization](docs/002-authorization.md)
- [003 Execution](docs/003-execution.md)
- [004 Prompts](docs/004-prompts.md)
- [005 Panel](docs/005-panel.md)
- [006 Deployment](docs/006-deployment.md): manual setup, configuration, upgrades and troubleshooting
- [007 Architecture](docs/007-architecture.md)

## Development

`pnpm check` runs the typecheck, the tests and the build.

# unslop

Created by Damir Sokolovsky ([@heydamir](https://x.com/heydamir)), who started the [Unslopping series](https://x.com/heydamir/status/2115063463063998736) on X.

![A vibecoded dashboard unslopping itself, frame by frame](skills/unslop/references/refs/story-dashboard-frames.webp)

unslop is a skill for Claude Code, Codex and Google Antigravity that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface with its own character. It finds the slop first, the purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, shouty copy and uneven spacing, then sets a direction from your product and fixes the screen pass by pass like a designer doing a redline review. It works in whatever your screen is built with, like Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML and CSS, on dashboards, apps and landing pages, and even on a live site when all you have is a link.

## Install

For Claude Code, install it as a plugin. Run this in a terminal to get it in every project:

```bash
claude plugin install unslop --marketplace heydamir/unslop
```

On an older Claude Code without `--marketplace`, the same in two steps:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add heydamir/unslop
claude plugin install unslop@heydamir
```

To get it in a single project only, run the install from that project's root folder, the one you start Claude Code in, and add `--scope local`. To turn it on for everyone who works in the project, add `--scope project` instead and commit `.claude/settings.json`. Each teammate then runs this once in their own copy of the project:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add heydamir/unslop
claude plugin install unslop@heydamir --scope project
```

Then start a new Claude Code session, or run `/reload-plugins` in one that is already open.

To update, run `claude plugin update unslop@heydamir`, or turn on auto-update for the heydamir marketplace under Marketplaces in `/plugin`.

If you copied unslop into `~/.claude/skills/` or a project's `.claude/skills/` before, delete that copy, or `/unslop` keeps running it instead of the plugin.

For Codex, ask it to install the skill straight from this repo.

```
$skill-installer install https://github.com/heydamir/unslop/tree/main/skills/unslop
```

Or copy it by hand into `~/.agents/skills/`, or into `.agents/skills/` inside a single project.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.agents/skills/
```

For Google Antigravity, copy the skill into your skills folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.gemini/config/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.gemini/config/skills/
```

For a single project, copy it into `.agents/skills/` inside that project instead.

To snapshot a live site or create a story video, install Playwright and its Chromium browser from the project directory where you run the skill:

```bash
npm install -D playwright
npx playwright install chromium
```

Story videos also require ffmpeg installed and available on your PATH.

## Use

In Claude Code, type `/unslop` with what you want, or `/unslop:unslop` if another skill already has that name. In Codex, type `$unslop` the same way. Or just ask in your own words and the agent picks the skill up by itself.

```
/unslop this dashboard
/unslop the hero of https://example.com
/unslop my landing page and make the story video so I can post it
```

It audits the screen and proposes a direction before it edits anything, so you can steer it early. If the screen is already good, it tells you so and suggests a few small refinements instead of redesigning it.

## What it does

- **Audit.** Lists every sign of slop with where it lives.
- **Direction.** Character, world, the one or two moments that carry the color, and a signature detail, all taken from your product.
- **Passes.** Spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion, in that order.

# Aerial **给国产电视的一块干净桌面。** 参照 Apple TV 做的 Android TV 桌面：没有广告，没有推荐流，只有你的 App、壁纸和航拍屏保。
适合小米、TCL、创维、索尼等国产电视，也能装在盒子和投影仪上。开机自动进入，待机也不会被清理。 **中文** · [English](README.en.md) ![Aerial 首页](site/img/home.jpg) | 电视自带的桌面 | 换上 Aerial 之后 | |:---:|:---:| | | |
## 功能

- **首页**：常用的一排 App 放在屏幕下方的玻璃底板上，往下是全部 App。小米「应用中心」「米家」这类藏起来的系统 App 也在。 - **整理**：长按 OK 键（或按菜单键）可以移动、放进文件夹、隐藏、卸载，或者设成「开机时打开」（开机、待机醒来直接进这个 App 或信号源）。固定到主屏幕的 HDMI 可以选接的是 Apple TV、PlayStation、Switch、Xbox、电脑等，换成对应的图标，也能在手机上起名字。 - **用手机整理**：扫电视上的二维码，手机上就是和电视一样的图标网格：按住拖动排序，点一下改名、换图标、放进文件夹或隐藏，也能把 HDMI 等信号源加到主屏幕。 - **图标库**：常用 App 直接用做好的 16:9 磁贴图，一个 App 可以有好几张，在手机上点开 App 挑，每张都写着来源。图来自 [le5inioo](https://github.com/le5inioo) 画的一套（[#706](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues/706)）、App 自己的 tvOS 版图标、Aerial 自己画的系统 App 图标和当贝桌面。 - **控制中心**：在第一排按上键到右上角打开，有信号源、网络、设置、音量、亮度和个性化。 - **屏保**：Apple TV 的 114 段航拍影片，电视支持时播 4K 或 4K 杜比视界，也可以换成照片、时钟或从手机添加的本地视频（[说明](docs/SCREENSAVER_VIDEOS.md)）。 - **壁纸**：必应每日精选、14 张内置壁纸、用手机扫码传的照片和视频，或者航拍：停在主屏幕 10 秒后在磁贴后面播放，按任意键停在当前画面。 - **个性化**：每排 4、5 或 6 个 App，单排或双排、时钟大小和位置、App 名称、焦点样式、按键声音，都能改。

repos._readme:
# Agent skills from Jane Street

A collection of skills for AI agents and chatbots.
Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` file
with instructions for the agent.

## Skills

- **socratic-tutor** — turns an LLM into a strict personal tutor that teaches a
  topic of your choice using the Socratic method: a diagnostic, a skill map with
  levels 0-5, one question at a time, spaced review, and a final assessment.

## How to use

With a coding agent that supports the common `SKILL.md` format, copy the skill
directory into your agent's skills folder, then ask the agent to use it
("teach me X").

With a plain chatbot, paste the body of the skill's `SKILL.md` into the chat
(or into a custom/system prompt), followed by what you want it to do.

## Contributing

These skills are exported from our internal repository, where we use them day to
day, and we hope it's interesting to share that experience more widely. Since
we're trying to share what _we've_ found to be useful, we're not looking for new
skills or for pull requests that change the text of existing ones. If you've
adapted a skill and it works better for you, that's great, but please keep your
own copy.

Issues are welcome if something doesn't work as described, though we may not be
able to act on all of them.

## Prior art

Teaching by asking questions is the
[Socratic method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socratic_method), which is
rather older than LLMs, and there are other tutoring prompts and skills built on
the same idea. Our skill was written internally and isn't knowingly derived from
any other implementation.

# Lichii [![Total downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/zortos293/Lichii/total)](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/releases) [![Latest release downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/zortos293/Lichii/latest/total)](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/releases) [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/zortos293/Lichii)](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/releases) Lichii is an experimental, open-source Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 emulator written in C++. It builds on Eglantine, Eden, yuzu and Sudachi, preserving their contributions while developing this fork's game compatibility and renderer fixes. This is an independent fork, not an official release of those upstream projects. Lichii is not affiliated with Nintendo. Visit the [Lichii game compatibility website](https://lichii.zortos.me) to find games and compare community compatibility reports. ## Downloads and setup Download Lichii only from this repository's [releases page](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/releases). Lichii has no other download site: archives offered elsewhere, such as lichii.org, are not built by this project, and one has been reported to install malware ([#545](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/issues/545)). On Windows, extract the entire build archive and run **lichii.exe**. Use homebrew you have permission to run, or your own games and system files dumped from a console you own, where permitted by applicable law. Games, keys and firmware are not included. The project does not provide download sources for them. Owning a console or game does not by itself establish permission to bypass access controls or redistribute its files. ### Existing saves and settings Lichii uses its own profile: `%APPDATA%\lichii` on Windows, and the `lichii` directories under `$XDG_DATA_HOME`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` on Linux and macOS. Without XDG overrides, these are `~/.local/share/lichii`, `~/.config/lichii` and `~/.cache/lichii`. An existing portable `user/` directory still takes priority and is not imported or changed by the wizard. On the first non-portable GUI launch, Lichii offers to import Eden and other detected emulator profiles. Back up `%APPDATA%\eden` first on Windows, or the old data, config and cache directories on Unix, and close the source emulator. Choose **Keep Old Data** to copy without changing the source, then check your saves and relaunch. Existing destination data is retained in backup directories rather than merged. Move also retains a source backup until you remove it yourself; Link deliberately shares settings and saves. Paths outside the imported data root remain shared and unchanged. An interrupted import offers recovery on the next launch. `eden-cli`, including `--help` and `--version`, refuses to initialize configuration until you import or explicitly choose **Start fresh** in the GUI. ## Compatibility and issue reports Compatibility and performance vary by game, hardware and driver. Rendering errors, stutters and crashes remain possible. Passing automated tests does not establish that a game renders correctly, and this project makes no universal frame-rate guarantee.
